app.tagline: A translation workbench for structured text
app.title: Corpus
catalogue.empty: No strings yet. Push a snapshot to populate this project.
catalogue.heading: Catalogue
editor.errorEmpty: Nothing to save: the translation is empty.
editor.errorInvalid: That translation was not saved: what is wrong is listed under the box, with your draft kept.
editor.errorSourceRow: The source text comes from the repository and is not edited here.
editor.formatChanged: {name} is a {type} in the source, not a {actual}
editor.formatDropped: {name} is a {type} in the source; write it with its format
editor.insertPlural: Insert a plural on {arg} with the branches {keys}
editor.insertSelect: Insert a select on {arg} with the keys {keys}
editor.insertTag: Insert the <{name}> tag, which the translation must keep
editor.pluralDropped: The source is a plural on {name}: write the translation as one
editor.chromeDollarLone: Chrome drops the lone $ with the character after it ({written}): write $$ for the sign
editor.chromeDollarPrice: Chrome reads {written} as substitution {digit} then {rest}: write ${written} for a price
editor.chromeDollarNamed: Chrome reads {written} as a $ before the placeholder, then reads that $ with the start of its value, so Bob shows as ob and $1 as a literal $1: put a space between, or the $ in the placeholder's content
editor.formCount: {actual, plural, one {# form reads} other {# forms read}} as {actualForms} under vue-i18n's default rule, where the source's {expected} are {expectedForms}
editor.formMeanings: Under vue-i18n's default rule, write as many forms as the source, shown for {forms}
editor.missingCategory: Plural {arg} is missing the {key} branch the runtime picks in this language
editor.fixedCount: The {key} branch of {arg} writes 1, but this language also picks it for {values}: write the count in it
editor.fixedCountMore: The {key} branch of {arg} writes 1, but this language also picks it for {values} and more: write the count in it
editor.overriddenBranch: Plural {arg} writes {key} and {category}, which gen-l10n reads as one branch: it keeps the one written later and drops the other
editor.wideExact: gen-l10n reads {key} on {arg} as {category}, which this language also picks for {values}: write {category} for what they share
editor.wideExactMore: gen-l10n reads {key} on {arg} as {category}, which this language also picks for {values} and more: write {category} for what they share
editor.wideExactOwn: gen-l10n reads {key} on {arg} as {category}, which this language also picks for {value}: write {category} for what they share, or give {value} its own ={value}
editor.missingPlaceholderQuoted: Missing {name}: an apostrophe before a brace quotes it, so write ’ in its place
editor.changedVerb: {actual} at position {name} is {expected} in the source; a verb that moved needs its index, {indexed}
editor.changedVerbType: {actual} at position {name} where the source has {expected}
editor.missingTagQuoted: Missing the <{name}> tag: an apostrophe before a tag quotes it, so write ’ in its place
editor.unpairedTag: <{name}> wraps nothing here, where the source's <{name}>…</{bare}> wraps text
editor.proofreading: Proofreading the source ({language}). Translations are edited from the untranslated and stale queues.
editor.selects: Insert a select or a plural
editor.staleBanner: The source text changed after this translation was saved. Check it against the source above, then save again.
editor.suggestionLabel: The repository's fuzzy guess, not yet a translation
editor.unexpectedCategory: Plural {arg} has a {key} branch the runtime never picks in this language
editor.movedPlaceholder: {name} is in the text where the source writes it inside {tag}; is the tag written wrong?
editor.unknownPlural: The source has no value {arg} to count
editor.countForMarker: {name} is dropped; %n shows the count in its place
editor.ordinalAsPlural: {arg} is a selectordinal in the source (1st, 2nd…): write it as one, not as a plural
editor.pluralAsOrdinal: {arg} is a plural in the source: write it as one, not as a selectordinal
editor.flattenedPlural: The plural on {arg} is written as one text, so every count reads the same form
editor.unpassedSelector: The source never passes {arg}, so Fluent shows this select's default
editor.unknownSelect: The source has no select on {arg}
editor.changedNesting: {inner} sits inside a branch of {outer}, where the source does not put it
editor.nestedCount: # in a select within the plural on {arg} is text to some runtimes; write the placeholder {arg} instead
editor.hashText: gen-l10n prints # as written: write {count} for the count
editor.bareAt: An @ that opens no link does not compile in vue-i18n, which then shows the message raw; write {literal}
editor.warningSourceChanged: The source changed since you opened this string. Your draft is kept below; read it against the new source before saving.
entities.empty: No entities yet. Push a snapshot that includes them.
entities.heading: Entities
entities.noMatches: No entities match. Clear the search or pick another type.
home.emptyMaintainer: Create a project, then push your repository's text into it from its root:
home.emptyTranslator: A maintainer creates a project and pushes the repository's text into it. There is nothing to translate until then.
invite.errorCredentials: That name and password were not accepted.
invite.errorInvalid: That invite secret was not accepted, or the name is empty.
invite.errorNameTaken: That name is taken. Sign in above, or pick another.
invite.errorRateLimited: Too many failed attempts. Try again in {minutes} min.
invite.errorWeakPassword: That password is too short. Use at least eight characters.
invite.heading: New here? Join with the invite secret
invite.intro: The instance invite secret lets you in once. Pick the display name your colleagues will see and a password of your own.
invite.passwordHint: At least {min} characters. A sentence works well.
newProject.errorInvalid: Check the fields: the slug is lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, languages are codes such as pt-PT, and they must include the source language.
newProject.heading: New project
newProject.languagesHint: Every language the project carries, the source language included, as codes separated by commas.
newProject.name: Name
newProject.nameHint: Shown to translators wherever the project is listed.
newProject.slugHint: The short name in the project's address, such as moonlight-manor: lowercase letters, digits and hyphens. It cannot change later.
newProject.sourceLanguageHint: The language the repository's text is written in, as a code such as pt-PT.
newProject.tokenOnce: Copy this push token now. It is shown only once.
notFound.description: This page does not exist. Check the address or go back home.
notFound.heading: Page not found
password.heading: Choose a new password
password.intro: Your new password replaces the current one on every device.
password.introReset: A maintainer reset your password. The temporary one you signed in with stops working once you save your own.
proposal.addErrorExists: A string with that key exists.
proposal.addErrorKey: That key is not a valid identifier.
proposal.addErrorSource: Pick one of the declared sources.
proposal.addKeyHint: Letters, digits, dots, underscores and hyphens; the id the repository will carry.
proposal.addNoSources: This project declares no source Corpus can write to. Push from a repository with a JSON catalogue first.
proposal.added: Proposed {key}. It reaches the repository with the next corpus pull.
proposal.errorForbidden: Only its author or a maintainer can withdraw a proposal.
proposal.errorNotPending: That proposal is no longer pending.
proposal.errorUnchanged: That is the current source text.
proposal.heading: Source proposals
proposal.invalidIcu: The text must parse as a source.
proposal.keyIsText: The text of this string is its key: change it in the code that calls t() or tr(), and the catalogue follows.
proposal.generated: This string is read from {file}, which is generated from the code: change the text in the code, and the next extract carries it.
proposal.generatedError: This string's source file is generated from the code: change the text in the code, and the next extract carries it.
proposal.notWritable: This string comes from a source Corpus cannot write back to (an exec command or a non-JSON catalogue), so its source is edited in the repository.
proposal.proposed: Proposed. It reaches the repository with the next corpus pull.
proposal.replaceHint: A newer proposal replaces the pending one.
settings.errorAgent: The agent actor never signs in and cannot be a maintainer.
settings.errorInvalid: Check the fields: languages are codes such as pt-PT.
settings.errorLastMaintainer: The instance needs at least one maintainer.
settings.heading: Settings
settings.historyEmpty: No pushes yet. Run corpus push from the project's repository.
settings.historyIntro: Every push from the CLI, newest first.
settings.languagesIntro: The source language is {language} and cannot change here.
settings.resetDone: Temporary password for {name}. Copy it now: it is shown once, their sessions have ended, and they will choose a new password at sign-in.
settings.targetLanguagesHint: Language codes separated by commas, such as pt-PT, en.
settings.tokenIntro: The CLI pushes with a per-project token. Rotating it invalidates the old one at once.
settings.tokenOnce: Copy this token now. It is shown once and disappears after a minute.
settings.usersIntro: Everyone who joined with the invite secret. Maintainers verify strings and change settings.
source.fluentMessage: The message {name}, as each language's own file defines it
string.archived: This string is archived. It is read-only.
string.richTextHtml: Every {type} string is read as HTML: a translation may write its own tags.
string.richTextHtmlKey: Rails reads this key as HTML, its name ending in _html: a translation's tags are its own markup, closed as the source closes them.
string.otherLanguagesMore: {count, plural, one {# more language} other {# more languages}}
string.siblingsCount: {shown} of {total} strings of this type under the same key prefix or in the same plural family
switcher.label: Select a project
verify.errorGeneric: This string could not be verified.
verify.warningChanged: This string changed since you opened it. Your sign-off applied to the latest version.
